sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: Date palm is a dioecious palm native from the Arabian Peninsula to southern Pakistan and cultivated in hot, dry regions. Its trunk can reach about 15–40 m.

sections.title: Fronds, flowers and fruit
sections.text: The crown often bears around a hundred pinnate fronds 4–7 m long; the basal leaflets become spines. Dates are one-seeded oblong berries whose size varies greatly among cultivars.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: The fruits are eaten fresh or dried. Unlike the Canary Island date palm, this species produces fleshy fruits widely cultivated as food.
